data.gender_notes: Hayaam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h.w.y, meaning 'to live'. In Islamic tradition, Hayaam is considered a spiritual name that symbolizes the continuity and importance of existence. The name Hayaam carries the meaning “Living, Existence” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hayaam usually hope their child will grow to embody living, existence and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hayaam total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: هيام
in_arabic.meaning: هيام اسم يعني شديد الحب أو الغرق في الحب
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم هيام مشتق من الجذر العربي (هـ ي م) الذي يعني الغرق في الحب أو الشوق. يستخدم الاسم في الثقافة العربية ليعبر عن الحب العميق أو الشوق الحار. ورد في بعض التفاسير أنه قد يعني أيضًا الذهاب في الحب أو التعلق الشديد.

in_urdu.name: ہیام
in_urdu.meaning: ہیام کا مطلب ہے پیار میں غرق ہونا یا شدید محبت
in_urdu.long_meaning: ہیام نام عربی جڑ (ہـ یـ م) سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے محبت میں ڈوب جانا یا شدید عشق۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں محبت یا پیار کی گہرائی کو ظاہر کرنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हयाम
in_hindi.meaning: हयाम का अर्थ है प्रेम में डूबना या गहन प्रेम
in_hindi.long_meaning: हयाम नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल (हـ यـ म) से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है प्रेम में डूब जाना या गहरा प्यार। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में प्रेम की गहराई या तीव्र स्नेह को व्यक्त करने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: هيام
in_pashto.meaning: هيام د ډېر مینې یا په مینه کې ډوبېدو مانا
in_pashto.long_meaning: هيام نوم د عربي ريښې (هـ يـ م) څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې مانا يې په مینه کې ډوبېدل یا شديد مینه. دا نوم د افغان او پښتني کلتور په دوديزو کې د مینې او پېار څرګندولو لپاره کارول کيږي.

This name is used in Islamic tradition to express deep love or longing. Etymologically, it relates to the concept of love and attachment in Arabic linguistic and cultural heritage.

data.cultural_impact: Hayaam is primarily identified as a masculine name in the Islamic world. It is worth noting that the wider Arabic word "hayy" (alive, living) is well-known and culturally significant in Eastern and Western literature, emphasizing the concept of life as a continuous journey and transformation. Many scholars and poets associated with Islamic culture have touched upon its significance, advocating for the appreciation and value of life.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hayaam holds more profound spiritual significance for Muslims. According to Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) used this name for a companion, Al-Aswad Al-Ansari, whose eyes had been blinded in a battle. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) gave him the name Hayaam because he believed that even though he had lost his physical sight, Al-Aswad had gained "spiritual sight," enabling him to live in the hereafter with a motivated spirit. The name thus represents a reminder of the importance of both temporal and spiritual lives, serving as an uplifting reminder and inspiration for individuals striving for personal growth and self-improvement.
